subject: maths
title: Shapes, Direction and Movement
introductionText:
Term 1 · Geometry
Shapes, Direction and Movement
The Big Idea: Flat shapes (2D) can be drawn on paper. Solid shapes (3D) can be held in
your hand. We tell them apart by counting sides and corners, and by looking for flat or
curved parts.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"Some shapes are flat, like a drawing — we call them 2D. A square has 4 straight sides, all
the same length, and 4 corners. A rectangle also has 4 sides and 4 corners, but two sides
are long and two are short, like a door. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. A circle is
round, with no corners at all. Shapes you can hold are 3D: a dice is a cube, a ball is a
sphere, a tin is a cylinder."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
Calling a 3D shape by its face's name. He calls a ball a "circle" and a dice a "square". Hold
up the dice: "This flat part is a square. The whole dice is a cube. Flat — square. Solid —
cube."
Thinking a turned square is a new shape. A square standing on its corner is often called a
"diamond". It still has 4 equal sides and 4 corners — it is still a square.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — Kitchen shape hunt (10 minutes)
Find one of each: a cube (sugar cube, dice), a cuboid (tissue box, cereal box), a cylinder
(tin, glass), a sphere (orange, ball), a cone (ice-cream cone, funnel). Put them on a tray.
Ask him to guess first: which will roll? which will stack? Then test each one on the floor.
Game 2 — Shape prints (5 minutes)
Press the bottom of a cup, a box and a dice into play dough (or trace around them on
paper). Which print does each make? The cup leaves a circle, the box a rectangle, the dice
a square. Then ask: could a ball leave a print with corners?
Flat (2D) shapes
circle triangle square rectangle
Solid (3D) shapes
cube cuboid sphere cylinder cone pyramid
Point to each shape and say its name, then find a matching object in the room together.
More examples to talk about
• A cylinder can roll and stack. A sphere only rolls. A cube only slides and stacks.
• A cone rolls round in a circle, not in a straight line — try it!
• The Pyramids of Giza are giant pyramids — the 3D shape is named after buildings like
them.
• Tricky: a slice of pizza looks like a triangle, but one side is curved, so it isn't really a
triangle.
• Tricky: a very long, thin square is impossible — if the sides aren't all equal, it's a
rectangle.
Key Words
2D 3D side corner face straight curved circle triangle square
rectangle cube cuboid sphere cylinder cone pyramid

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write the name under each shape.
I have 4 corners and 4 equal sides. What am I?
I have 6 square faces and 8 corners. What am I?
A triangle has sides and corners.

Circle the shapes that can roll:
sphere cube cylinder cuboid

Sort these into the table: square, ball, tin, triangle, dice, circle
Flat (2D) Solid (3D)
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: 2D: square, triangle, circle • 3D: ball, tin, dice

sourceQuestions.sourceText: True or false? A square turned onto its corner is still a square.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: True. It still has 4 equal sides and 4 corners.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Draw a house using squares, rectangles and triangles. How many triangles did you use?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any house built from the named shapes; the number of triangles must match his drawing.
